questions.prompt: A page has one primary content area. Which element should identify it?

options.text: A single <main> element for the page's dominant content
A <section> with role="main" even when a native <main> is available
A <div> with an accessible name but no landmark role
A <main> around each independently navigable article

questions.prompt: When is an ARIA role most appropriate for a control?

options.text: Whenever a native element already exposes the same role, to make it explicit
When native HTML cannot express the needed semantics and the role's behavior and states are also implemented
As a replacement for keyboard interaction on a custom clickable <div>
When visual styling should determine what assistive technology announces

questions.prompt: Which markup gives this input a programmatic label that remains associated when the text is clicked?

options.text: The input's placeholder supplies a persistent accessible label
The input type alone provides the label 'Email'
The matching label for and input id create the explicit association
A title on the form is inherited as every control's label

questions.prompt: A checkout rejects orders above a customer's authorized limit. Where must that rule be enforced?

options.text: Only with a client-side max attribute because the browser blocks larger values
Only with JavaScript before the form is submitted
With required and pattern attributes, which prevent crafted requests
On the server, with optional client-side checks used for faster feedback

questions.prompt: A form needs to submit an uneditable account identifier. Which control behavior preserves it in the form submission?

options.text: Use a supported readonly control; disabled controls are not successful form controls
Use disabled, because disabled values are included but cannot be changed
Omit the name attribute so the browser submits the control's id
Use hidden input and treat its value as trusted because it is not visible

questions.prompt: A document at /shop/items/ links to ../images/item.png. Which URL path does the browser resolve?

options.text: /images/item.png
/shop/images/item.png
/shop/items/images/item.png
/shop/items/../images/item.png without URL resolution

questions.prompt: A trusted external documentation link opens a new browsing context. Which statement about opener protection is accurate?

options.text: target="_blank" always requires JavaScript to prevent the destination from controlling its opener
rel="nofollow" alone blocks access to window.opener
rel="noopener" is the relevant explicit protection; modern browsers also generally imply it for _blank
rel="noreferrer" preserves the referrer while disabling opener access

questions.prompt: For width-descriptor srcset candidates, what does sizes tell the browser?

options.text: The maximum intrinsic width allowed for the source image
Which image format should be decoded first
The CSS width to force on the rendered image
The expected rendered slot width, helping choose a candidate with the device pixel ratio

questions.prompt: What is the role of the img element in this responsive image pattern?

options.text: It supplies the fallback image and the image's alternative text
It is used only when the picture contains no source elements
It turns the source media query into a CSS breakpoint
It provides an image caption automatically from its alt text

questions.prompt: For prerecorded speech with meaningful speaker changes and sound cues, which track kind best meets deaf and hard-of-hearing users' needs?

options.text: metadata, because it labels the video for search engines
captions, with synchronized text for dialogue and relevant non-speech audio
chapters, because chapter titles replace synchronized text
descriptions, because an audio description track is equivalent to captions

questions.prompt: A large image is the page's likely Largest Contentful Paint element. Which loading choice is the best starting point?

options.text: Always set loading="lazy" because every image should wait until scrolling
Remove intrinsic dimensions so the browser can discover the final size after download
Keep it discoverable and eager; consider high fetch priority only when measurement supports it
Preload every image on the page to eliminate image contention

questions.prompt: For a classic external script that depends on parsed DOM and must preserve order relative to other deferred scripts, which attribute is appropriate?

options.text: async, which guarantees document order after parsing
blocking, which downloads in parallel and runs after parsing
preconnect, which schedules script execution after DOM construction
defer, which downloads without blocking parsing and runs after parsing in document order

questions.prompt: A third-party script is independent of page scripts and may execute as soon as its download completes. What is the key trade-off of async?

options.text: It avoids parser blocking during download, but execution timing and order relative to other async scripts are not guaranteed
It guarantees execution after DOMContentLoaded and preserves source order
It prevents the script from running until the user interacts
It causes the browser to fetch the script only after all images finish

questions.prompt: A page knows it will fetch a critical stylesheet from a new CDN origin. Which hint can start connection setup early without naming a particular file?

options.text: prefetch, which establishes TLS immediately for any future origin
preconnect to the CDN origin, used selectively because it has setup cost
preload without an href, which discovers the stylesheet automatically
dns-prefetch, which guarantees the stylesheet is fetched and parsed

questions.prompt: What condition most directly supports reliable hydration of server-rendered markup?

options.text: The client always replaces the server DOM before users can see it
The server emits no semantic HTML so the client can invent structure later
The initial client render agrees with the server-rendered structure and relevant content
Every server response contains exactly the same personalized data for all users

questions.prompt: Where can non-whitespace text placed directly inside a table end up after HTML parsing?

options.text: It is always discarded as invalid source text
It remains a text child between table rows in every browser
It becomes the accessible name of the table automatically
The HTML parser can foster-parent it outside the table

questions.prompt: What happens to this content before it is cloned or otherwise inserted into the document?

options.text: Its contents are held in an inert template fragment and are not rendered as part of the page
The button is rendered but cannot receive focus
The browser immediately inserts the button after the template
The template is a server-side include that runs on every browser

questions.prompt: What native behavior does this markup provide without custom JavaScript?

options.text: A modal dialog that makes the rest of the document inert
A disclosure whose summary toggles visibility of the remaining details content
A form section that is automatically submitted when opened
A disclosure that requires an aria-expanded attribute to function

questions.prompt: Which statement distinguishes dialog.showModal() from dialog.show()?

options.text: Both methods always create a modal and make the page inert
showModal() only changes a CSS class and has no built-in focus behavior
showModal() presents the dialog modally in the top layer; show() opens it non-modally
show() is required for every dialog element to appear in the document

questions.prompt: What naming requirement applies when defining an autonomous custom element?

options.text: Its name must start with the prefix html-
Its name must match a built-in element such as article
Its name must contain an uppercase letter to distinguish it from HTML
Its valid custom-element name includes a hyphen and avoids reserved names

questions.prompt: Which statement about a Shadow DOM tree is accurate?

options.text: It offers component-oriented DOM and style scoping, but it is not a security boundary
It prevents all page scripts from inspecting or affecting component behavior
It automatically makes every control inside accessible to keyboard users
It guarantees that component styles cannot inherit or interact with page-level styling

questions.prompt: What can a standards-based HTML conformance checker establish about a document?

options.text: That every user agent will render it pixel-identically
That it conforms to checked HTML rules, but not that it is fully accessible or usable
That no manual accessibility review is necessary
That all server-side form validation rules are enforced

questions.prompt: An API returns a user-controlled string for display. Which DOM operation treats it as text rather than parsing it as markup?

options.text: Set innerHTML to the value after checking that it looks like a sentence
Put the value in an event-handler attribute so the browser escapes it
Assign the value to textContent on the paragraph element
Use document.write after the page has loaded

questions.prompt: Which document architecture best supports maintainable pages with shared layout and varied content?

options.text: Copy a separate full document for every page so shared regions can drift independently
Place all content in one generic div and infer meaning from CSS classes
Use runtime fetches to assemble critical page landmarks after every navigation
Use reusable templates for shared structure and semantic elements for each page's content roles

questions.prompt: Which practices generally improve accessible semantics without adding redundant ARIA?

options.text: Use native buttons for actions and links for navigation
Add role="button" to every native button to reinforce its role
Give form controls persistent, programmatic labels
Use aria-label on every element, including elements that already have a clear accessible name

questions.prompt: Which statements about form contracts and validation are correct?

options.text: A successful control generally needs a name and must not be disabled to contribute its value
Server-side validation remains necessary even when native constraint validation is used
A required attribute guarantees that a crafted HTTP request contains a valid value
Client-side validation can mirror useful rules to give earlier, more actionable feedback

questions.prompt: Which practices are sound when authoring links and URLs?

options.text: Assume every relative URL is resolved against the site's origin root
Choose link text that communicates the destination or action without relying only on surrounding visual context
Account for the document base URL when resolving relative references
Use target="_blank" on every link so browser history remains predictable

questions.prompt: Which statements describe responsive-image markup accurately?

options.text: Use width-descriptor srcset with an appropriate sizes description when candidate choice depends on layout width
Use sizes as a replacement for CSS sizing and layout rules
Use alt text to describe an image's purpose in context, or empty alt when it is purely decorative
Use picture sources for cases such as art direction or format-specific alternatives, retaining an img fallback

questions.prompt: Which choices can help reduce rendering instability or unnecessary network work?

options.text: Declare image dimensions or an aspect ratio to reserve layout space
Lazy-load below-the-fold images when delaying their fetch is appropriate
Preload every image and stylesheet so discovery order no longer matters
Avoid lazy-loading a likely above-the-fold LCP image without a measured reason

questions.prompt: Which statements about script attributes and resource hints are accurate?

options.text: Classic async scripts are guaranteed to execute in document order
Classic deferred scripts execute after document parsing and preserve their relative order
preconnect fetches and parses a named stylesheet before the parser discovers it
preload targets a specific resource; its destination and later use should be compatible

questions.prompt: Which statements distinguish common rendering strategies accurately?

options.text: Static-site generation emits HTML at build time for content that can be prepared then
Server rendering inherently guarantees that the client can hydrate without matching output
Hydration adds client-side behavior to server-rendered markup and depends on a compatible initial render
Client-side rendering means the browser never constructs a DOM from HTML

questions.prompt: Why can the parsed DOM differ from a literal reading of malformed HTML source?

options.text: The HTML parser applies defined error-recovery and tree-construction rules
The DOM is always a byte-for-byte representation of the source file
Duplicate attributes are preserved as independent DOM attributes in every user agent
Certain invalid table-context content can be foster-parented during parsing

questions.prompt: Which statements correctly describe native disclosure, dialog, and template elements?

options.text: details with summary provides a built-in disclosure interaction
dialog.showModal() creates a modal presentation distinct from dialog.show()
template contents are not rendered as ordinary document content until inserted
The presence of a template element automatically clones its contents each time a custom event fires

questions.prompt: Which statements about custom elements and Shadow DOM are accurate?

options.text: Custom element names have syntax requirements, including a hyphen for autonomous custom elements
A shadow root makes its contents a security sandbox for secrets
Shadow DOM can scope component structure and styles while exposing deliberate composition points
A custom element automatically receives correct keyboard behavior for any custom interaction

questions.prompt: Which actions belong in a reliable HTML and accessibility validation workflow?

options.text: Treat a clean validator result as proof that the interface is usable with assistive technology
Use an HTML conformance checker to catch markup and authoring errors
Assume an automated accessibility scan detects every keyboard and screen-reader issue
Combine automated checks with keyboard, zoom, and assistive-technology evaluation of critical flows

questions.prompt: Which practices help keep HTML architecture safer and easier to maintain?

options.text: Render untrusted plain text with textContent rather than parsing it as HTML
Repeat shared navigation and footer markup independently on every page to avoid template coupling
Use reusable templates for shared document structure and semantic landmarks for page-specific content
If untrusted rich HTML is required, apply a maintained sanitizer and narrowly scoped allow-list policy

questions.prompt: Match each interface need to the most appropriate semantic HTML pattern.

rows.label: Identify the page's dominant content region
Hide a purely decorative image from the text alternative
Perform an in-page action when activated
Reveal or hide a related block of details

questions.prompt: For each form requirement, select the best primary mechanism. Server-side validation remains necessary for submitted data.

rows.label: Reject a missing value early in a normal browser form
Enforce an authoritative account-specific spending limit
Associate visible text with a control
Submit a non-editable value for a supported text control

columns.label: Validate the domain rule on the server
Associate label for with the control id

questions.prompt: Match each responsive-media requirement to the HTML mechanism that directly supports it.

rows.label: Choose image candidates based on layout slot width
Select a different crop at a viewport breakpoint
Offer format-specific image sources with fallback
Provide synchronized text for dialogue and relevant sounds

columns.label: picture source with a media condition
picture source with a type condition and img fallback
A captions track for the media

questions.prompt: Match each loading need to the most appropriate script or resource-hint mechanism.

rows.label: Classic external code needs parsed DOM and must retain relative order
Independent classic code may execute as soon as it is ready
Warm up a known cross-origin connection without selecting a file
Request a specific critical resource before normal discovery

questions.prompt: Match each DOM or parsing goal to the operation or behavior that best describes it.

rows.label: Turn an HTML string into nodes using HTML parsing rules
Store markup without rendering it as ordinary page content
Insert untrusted text without interpreting it as markup
Create a known element without parsing an HTML string

questions.prompt: Match each delivery description to the rendering strategy it most directly describes.

rows.label: Generate document HTML on the server for each request
Generate reusable document HTML during the build
Build most of the interface in the browser after JavaScript runs
Attach client behavior to server-rendered markup
